text: AMG, factorizations, eigenvalues and quadrature Small fixed inputs connect numerical methods, references, errors, refinement and explicit failure conditions. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-foundations-2026-11-22 from the ZIP. This command executes all 4 fixed cases in the supplement. Choose a new or empty output directory. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Matrix-based AMG: distinguish residual and solution error Build a smoothed-aggregation hierarchy from an SPD matrix alone and run V-cycles. Problems with 7², 15² and 31² unknowns distinguish independent sparse direct solutions, analytic discrete sine modes and second-order convergence to the continuum solution. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless unit square, constant-positive-coefficient −Δu=f, homogeneous Dirichlet boundaries and five-point differences. Hierarchy setup receives no coordinates, mesh width or n; it uses the coefficient matrix and an implicit constant near-null candidate. A real SPD input is assumed; arbitrary indefinite problems are outside scope. Adopted numerical method A graph based on row-relative off-diagonal strength supplies greedy star aggregates; leftover nodes attach to adjacent aggregates. Smooth tentative T via P=(I−ωD⁻¹A)T with ω=4/(3ρ̄), where ρ̄ bounds the absolute row sums of D⁻¹A. Coarse operators are PᵀAP. V-cycles use two pre/post Jacobi sweeps and a terminal dense direct solve. This is a small adopted SA variant, not every construction or convergence theorem in the original paper. A randomly permuted matrix is also checked against a direct solution to expose hidden geometric ordering assumptions. A zero cycle budget reports nonconvergence. Verification limits and failures Only three fixed scalar grids are checked. Large coefficient jumps, strong anisotropy, elasticity, arbitrary unstructured meshes, optimal complexity and mesh-independent convergence are not certified. Algebraic multigrid by smoothed aggregation for second and fourth order elliptic problems · DOI: 10.1007/BF02238511 Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata Official reference-implementation documentation: scipy.sparse.linalg.spsolve.html Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD: orthogonality, rank and least squares Original Householder QR and one-sided Jacobi SVD for real tall matrices are checked on ordinary, 10⁶-column-scaled and rank-deficient inputs, against separate LAPACK singular values and minimum-norm least-squares solutions. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Small real matrices with m≥n. Numerical rank uses a 10⁻¹² threshold relative to the largest singular value; compact factors omit null directions. QR has no column pivoting and is not used as a rank-revealing method. Adopted numerical method Householder reflectors triangularize R while accumulating Q. The SVD repeatedly rotates column pairs toward orthogonality and uses their resulting lengths as singular values; it does not diagonalize AᵀA. Least squares uses triangular back substitution for QR and truncated compact SVD for deficient rank. Singular-vector signs are not compared; zero matrices and budget exhaustion are tested. Verification limits and failures Not a full LAPACK replacement or validation of complex/wide matrices, arbitrary extreme scales or optimal relative singular-value accuracy. The 10⁻¹² cutoff defines numerical rather than exact mathematical rank. The experiment does not establish all hypotheses of the Demmel–Veselić accuracy results. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries The symmetric case is real symmetric; the nonsymmetric case is real with a known separated largest eigenvalue 5. Starting vectors use fixed seeds. Nonsymmetric Ritz values may be complex and are selected by largest real part. Adopted numerical method Lanczos uses its three-term recurrence plus two passes of full reorthogonalization; Arnoldi uses two-pass modified Gram–Schmidt. Only the small projected T/H is solved by NumPy eigh/eig before lifting Ritz vectors. A full dense solve of the original matrix is used only on the reference side. Nonsymmetric Ritz convergence is not assumed monotone. Tests include identity-matrix happy breakdown, zero-start rejection and insufficient dimension budgets. Verification limits and failures Unrestarted small-matrix educational examples with separated extreme eigenpairs. Interior/clustered eigenvalues, very large sparse matrices, strong nonnormality, shift-invert and implicitly restarted Arnoldi are outside scope. A small eigenpair residual alone is not treated as a rigorous eigenvalue-error bound for nonnormal matrices. Stored measurements and decisions Display values are rounded. Variations on Arnoldi’s method for computing eigenelements of large unsymmetric matrices · DOI: 10.1016/0024-3795(80)90169-X Review scope / review_level: publisher-abstract-and-metadata Official reference-implementation documentation: scipy.linalg.eigh.html · scipy.linalg.eig.html Gauss–Legendre and adaptive quadrature: exactness, error estimates and budgets Construct Gaussian nodes/weights from the Legendre recurrence and test polynomial moments through degree 2n−1 and an exponential. Adaptive Simpson integrates exponential and Lorentzian peaks, against analytic integrals and independent QUADPACK. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Dimensionless smooth real functions on finite intervals. Fixed Gauss orders 2/4/8/16 and adaptive absolute tolerances 10⁻⁵/10⁻⁷/10⁻⁹ are swept separately. Endpoint singularities, discontinuities and infinite intervals are not covered by these inputs. Adopted numerical method Golub–Welsch obtains nodes from a symmetric Jacobi matrix and weights from twice the squared first eigenvector components. Adaptive Simpson bisects intervals and allocates tolerances using |Sleft+Sright−Swhole|/15 as a local estimate. Evaluation and depth limits report unmet targets explicitly. ∫−11f(x) dx≃∑j=1nwjf(xj)∫−11​f(x)dx≃j=1∑n​wj​f(xj​) Eest=∣Sleft+Sright−Swhole∣/15Eest​=∣Sleft​+Sright​−Swhole​∣/15 References and measured quantities Measure polynomial moments for every chosen order, node/weight differences from SciPy roots_legendre, order refinement for the analytic exponential integral, and agreement with analytic arctangent and SciPy quad references. Store evaluation counts/errors as tolerance tightens; test forced exhaustion after five evaluations and nonfinite integrands. Verification limits and failures The local Simpson estimate is not a rigorous error bound for arbitrary functions. The implementation does not generally solve missed high frequencies, singularities or roundoff stagnation, and it is not a reimplementation of Gauss–Kronrod or all of QUADPACK.
